propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when a model id contains a colon in its version suffix (canonical Bedrock ids like 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0'), because _resolve_target incorrectly treats any colon as a provider-qualifier separator.

The qualified/unqualified decision must be centralized in a single helper function (split_provider_qualifier) to prevent two independent and divergent implementations (infer_provider and _resolve_target) from reaching different conclusions.
An explicitly configured provider must be checked and honored before scanning the model string, so that no punctuation in a model id can overrule a direct configuration.
Conflicting provider qualifiers (explicit config vs inline qualifier in model string) must raise LLMConfigError rather than silently pick a winner, since both choices discard an explicit instruction.

The qualifier detection must distinguish valid provider names (identifiers: lowercase, digits, underscore, hyphen, no dots) from Bedrock model id fragments (which contain dots) rather than relying solely on colon position.
